3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.

373	CASE OD2-HO-KNOWN-1 (KNOWN, technical): Android login success drop at Oxleigh Mutual
374	Setting: Oxleigh Mutual is a fictional mid-sized retail bank with about 1.2 million mobile-app customers. Its Android and iOS apps call a mobile API that sits behind a vendor-managed edge protection service supplied by Corvane. Customers log in either by typing a password or by biometric/PIN quick-unlock on a device they have already enrolled. A product analytics team reports login success rates from in-app telemetry.
375	Presenting request: The Head of Digital Channels asks why Android login success has dropped since 3 March and what the bank should do now. She expects a rollback plan for Android release 6.14 by Thursday.
376	INITIAL EVIDENCE
377	E1 [stage S1] Email from Priya Lindqvist, Head of Digital Channels, 10 March (leadership-account): Team — Android login success has fallen off a cliff. Seven-day average was 97.1% for 24 Feb–2 Mar and 88.7% for 3–9 Mar. iOS is flat (97.4% to 97.3%) and web is flat (96.8% to 96.9%). The Android store rating for this week is 3.1, down from 4.4. Android 6.14 started rolling out on 3 March with the new password screen, and the timing speaks for itself. I want a rollback plan on my desk by Thursday and a clear explanation for the executive committee. Please don't spend a week on analysis; customers are locked out now.
378	E2 [stage S1] Notes from Tomás Reyes, Android engineering lead, 9 March (manager-account): 6.14 staged rollout began 3 Mar 09:00 UTC via the store console. Changes: redesigned password-login screen; our networking library nettle-http bumped from 4.11 to 4.12 (the Android app uses nettle-http for every API call); new analytics events. Crash-free sessions unchanged. The extra failures seem to be in password logins; biometric/PIN quick-unlock looks normal. We could not reproduce on our test devices against staging. Worth noting the March Android security patch started reaching phones around 2 March, and in 2024 an OS update broke keystore-backed login for us for two weeks. Can't rule either out yet.
379	E3 [stage S1] Change calendar extract, production, 2–4 March (change-record): CHG-5521 | 2 Mar 22:00 UTC | Core banking database index maintenance. Closed, no incidents.
380	CHG-5530 | 3 Mar 09:00 UTC | Android app 6.14 staged rollout start (store console). Owner: Mobile.
381	CHG-5534 | 3 Mar, vendor window | Edge protection (Corvane): vendor-managed rule pack auto-update to 2026.03.1. Standard change, pre-approved, applied by vendor; no bank testing required.
382	CHG-5536 | 3 Mar 14:00 UTC | Auth service: session-token lifetime for all mobile client IDs (iOS and Android) reduced from 30 to 20 minutes. Affects session expiry only.
383	CHG-5540 | 4 Mar 08:00 UTC | Marketing website TLS certificate renewal.
384	E4 [stage S1] Message from Dana Okafor, Security Operations manager, 9 March (manager-account): On 28 Feb we stopped a credential-stuffing run against web login. My read is that the Android drop is the same crowd moving onto the mobile API: bots fail logins, the success rate goes down. Two asks: (1) exclude edge-blocked attempts from the login KPI, because those are not real customers and they are distorting the number executives see; (2) raise Corvane bot-protection sensitivity on all login endpoints from 'standard' to 'high' until this blows over. Happy to brief the executive committee.
385	E5 [stage S1] Digital analytics KPI definition: mobile login success rate (v3, January) (document): Login success rate = login-success events ÷ login-attempt events, both emitted by the in-app telemetry SDK. An attempt event is emitted when a user submits a password or triggers biometric/PIN quick-unlock in an installed copy of the app. Each event carries an app-install ID, app version, OS version and an outcome category: success, credentials rejected, request rejected by server, or network/timeout. Requests sent to the API by scripts or tools other than the installed app do not emit telemetry events and are not counted. Dashboard tiles show the platform-level rate only.
386	E6 [stage S1] Contact-centre weekly operations summary, week of 2 March (system-record): Inbound calls 2–8 March: 41,200 against a four-week average of 34,900 (+18%). Average wait 6m40s (target 3m). Scheduled events this week: annual account-fee notices mailed 2 March to 610,000 customers; savings-rate change emailed 4 March. Reason coding: 57% of calls logged as 'General enquiry', the default code; a January coding audit found reason codes unreliable for trend analysis. Team leads report 'a mix of fee questions and people who can't get into the app'.

rulings.explanation: H5 claims the redesigned screen makes customers enter wrong credentials more often. It does not claim the screen caused the login drop. rulings.explanation: 'Unknown' needs evidence too weak to show even association, and that bar is not met. The 18% call rise is in the same week as the login drop (E6). Team leads report callers 'who can't get into the app' (E6). 'Digital access' calls are up 900, and 38 of 200 audited general enquiries are about app or online access (C8). A C9 reviewer says they could not log in and then called the bank. The fee-notice confounder and unreliable reason coding stop us apportioning the rise or establishing that the login drop caused it. That rules out 'causal'. Those problems affect attribution, not co-occurrence, which the evidence shows directly. 'Association-only' is the only defensible label.
